children: Canada's employment drop in August could reflect a "normalization" in data after three strong months of hiring, says Royce Mendes, head of macro strategy at Desjardins Capital Markets. In the May-to-July period, Canada added 181,100 jobs, or an average of over 60,000 per month. Mendes says it's possible some of the weakness may reflect the later-than-usual Labor Day weekend, "which could have pushed some of the typical end-of-summer hiring into September."
